raw_response:
I've been working this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou's soil — it's the North China Plain, good loam, but you have to keep it fed. With 10 mouths and some kids working in town sending money back, I need the crops to perform without overspending on inputs.

My 12 mu all runs wheat-maize rotation. That's how everyone here does it, and it makes sense — the wheat fixes the calendar and the maize fills out the income. I don't split the land; all 12 mu goes through both crops each year.

**Wheat (autumn planting, June harvest):** I'll use the improved Jimai variety my neighbor has been using — good lodging resistance and the county extension office pushed it a few years ago. Three irrigations: one at sowing to ensure germination, one at jointing, one at heading. I don't bother with a fourth — costs money and my well yield isn't unlimited. Two pesticide runs: one herbicide pass in winter, one fungicide/insecticide spray at heading for powdery mildew and aphids. After the maize comes off in October, I do rotary tillage to break up the stubble before planting. Yield should be around 450 kg/mu — that's what I get in a normal year.

**Maize (June planting, October harvest):** Hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or similar — hybrids have been standard here for 20 years, no reason to go back. After wheat harvest I'll direct-seed without tilling — saves diesel and time, and the soil doesn't need turning again so soon. Two irrigations: one at jointing, one at tasseling and silking — that's the critical window. Two pesticide applications: herbicide early on, then something for corn borer mid-season. Yield around 550 kg/mu.
